prompt: Two parallel crosswalk stripes are cut by a straight curb line acting as a transversal. One angle OUTSIDE the stripes measures $118^\circ$. What is the measure, in degrees, of its alternate exterior angle?
hint: Alternate exterior angles sit outside the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal.

hints.text: Alternate exterior angles sit outside the parallel lines, on opposite sides of the transversal.
With parallel lines, alternate exterior angles are congruent.
The alternate exterior angle is also $118^\circ$.

explanation: Alternate exterior angles lie outside the two parallel lines and on opposite sides of the transversal.
When the lines are parallel, they are congruent.
So the matching angle also measures $118^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Chain it through a vertical angle
steps: The $118^\circ$ angle has a vertical angle of $118^\circ$ at the same crossing, sitting inside the stripes.
That interior angle has an alternate interior partner of $118^\circ$ at the other crossing, whose vertical angle is the exterior angle you want: $118^\circ$.
